name: Diagnostic_VEC-SCP_1

functions.name: texp
functions.body: if numberp(x) and x<0 then concat("\\left(",tex1(x),"\\right)") else tex1(x)

functions.name: texsumf
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], concat("+",texp(t))), rest(L)))))

functions.name: texnsum
functions.body: block([L:first(args(e))], concat(tex1(first(L)), apply(sconcat, map(lambda([t], if numberp(t) and t<0 then concat("-",tex1(-t)) else concat("+",tex1(t))), rest(L)))))

questiontext:
Given that \(\mathbf{a} = {{CT:0}}\,\mathbf{i} + {{CT:1}}\,\mathbf{j} + {{CT:2}}\,\mathbf{k}\) and that \(\mathbf{b} = {{CT:3}}\,\mathbf{i} + {{CT:4}}\,\mathbf{j} + {{CT:5}}\,\mathbf{k}\)

then the scalar or "dot" product

\(\mathbf{a}.\mathbf{b}=\) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The scalar product is computed by multiplying the \(\mathbf{i}\), \(\mathbf{j}\) and \(\mathbf{k}\) components together and adding the three products: \(\mathbf{a}.\mathbf{b}=a_xb_x+a_yb_y+a_zb_z\).
Step 1 — The products of the components
With

\[ \mathbf{a} = {{CT:0}}\,\mathbf{i} + {{CT:1}}\,\mathbf{j} + {{CT:2}}\,\mathbf{k},\qquad \mathbf{b} = {{CT:3}}\,\mathbf{i} + {{CT:4}}\,\mathbf{j} + {{CT:5}}\,\mathbf{k} \]

the products of corresponding components are

\[ a_xb_x={{CT:6}}={{CT:7}},\qquad a_yb_y={{CT:8}}={{CT:9}},\qquad a_zb_z={{CT:10}}={{CT:11}}. \]

Step 2 — Adding
The scalar product is the sum of these products (a number, not a vector):

\[ \mathbf{a}.\mathbf{b}={{CT:12}}={{CT:13}}. \]

on_true.feedback: You appear to have added together the components of the vector product.
